title: Tenant telemetry mux rotation and span reassembly after cross-mode routing regression
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a weekend incident multiple customers (mix of Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments) reported missing time-series on platform dashboards and truncated traces. The root failure path tied to a telemetry-router edge-case introduced in the traffic-multiplexing change: when a tenant had both dedicated pools and hosted fallbacks, the router rotated to a deprecated mux slot which caused metric shards to be tombstoned and span-linker to drop span parent references for sampled traces. Impact included broken SLO dashboards, alert noise suppression failures, and elevated support escalations.

Why this ticket: We need a surgical production patch to fix the router mux rotation logic, a safe reassembly approach to relink orphan spans, a backfill for missing metrics where possible, and postmortem + automated tests to prevent regression.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a tenant with one Dedicated pool and Hosted fallback. 2) Generate mixed traffic with both short-lived sessions and long replies to exercise KV cache rotation. 3) Apply the previous release’s mux rotation config (patched in runtime-1.17) and observe metrics TTL tombstones in /metrics-tenant/{tenant}/shard. 4) Inspect traces for missing parent_id headers on sampled spans in the last 3 minutes. 5) Note dashboard livepanels showing zeros for ingestion windows overlapping the mux rotation window.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers experienced blank dashboard tiles and degraded trace continuity for 15-40 minutes during the incident window. Two customers opened P1 escalations; one customer delayed a production rollout because alerts were silent. Observable consequence: SLO burn and increased support time until mitigation engaged.
commits: c3a1b7d: fix(router): guard mux-rotation against deprecated-slot selection
f7e2d9a: fix(trace-linker): tolerant relinking for orphan spans
root_cause: A regression in the telemetry-router mux rotation selector (introduced to improve latency balancing) did not account for tenants with mixed routing policies. Under a specific interleaving of KV cache compaction and slot rewrap, metric shard IDs were marked as tombstoned instead of migrated to the new slot. The trace-linker module relied on consistent shard metadata; when metadata was missing the linker dropped parent references, producing orphaned spans.
resolution: 1) Hotfix applied to telemetry-router to ignore deprecated mux slots under mixed-routing flag (rolled out to canary-hosted and two Dedicated pools). 2) Trace-linker patched to attempt two-phase reassembly: consult recent shard-alias map before dropping parent refs and emit a sparse diagnostic span for tracing continuity. 3) Backfill job created to rehydrate tombstoned metric shards for affected tenants using write-ahead logs and prefix-cache snapshots. 4) Alerts updated to detect tombstone spikes and automatically widen sampling for traces during migration windows.
timeline: 2026-03-01 02:18 UTC: PagerDuty triggered from blank dashboard alert. 2026-03-01 02:34 UTC: Investigation identified elevated tombstone counts in telemetry-router logs. 2026-03-01 03:10 UTC: Canary patch deployed to canary-hosted. 2026-03-01 03:42 UTC: Patch promoted to Dedicated and Private customer pools. 2026-03-01 05:00 UTC: Backfill job started; partial rehydration completed by 2026-03-01 08:45 UTC. 2026-03-01 11:00 UTC: Customer escalations closed with RCA summary and mitigation notes.
qa_and_test_plan: - Add unit tests covering mux rotation when tenant.routing_policy == mixed. - Add integration test that simulates KV cache compaction during rotation and asserts no tombstones are produced. - Add e2e scenario in staging that runs trace continuity checker across a 1-hour simulated migration window. - Validate backfill idempotency in a dry-run cluster before executing in prod.
rollback_plan: If hotfix causes regressions: revert the telemetry-router change and switch affected tenants to explicit routing policy 'hosted-only' or 'dedicated-only' as a temporary mitigation; pause backfill; apply emergency config to disable rotation window for the tenant; communicate with any impacted customers and open follow-up remediation tickets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No tombstone spike in the telemetry-router after rotation in canary and two Dedicated test tenants. 2) Trace continuity metric (span-continuity-rate) returns to baseline within 2x during a test window. 3) Backfill successfully rehydrates >95% of missing metric points for affected tenants in dry-run. 4) PRs merged and release notes published to console-2026.03 with customer-facing RCA.
followups: ENG-853680: observability - add tombstone spike automated rollback policy
PM-412: customer communications and SLA credit proposal
ENG-853681: infra - make backfill multi-tenant safe and throttled
notes: We observed the issue most frequently for tenants with >3 active pools and a mix of short TTL caches. The patch is intentionally conservative — it prefers stability over aggressive rotation and adds telemetry so we can confidently tighten later. Customer comms drafted in PM-412. Security review: not required for the code changes but backfill touches raw metrics so access logs are retained.
